Practice Note for Authorized Persons,
 Buildings Department    Registered Structural Engineers and       ADV-29
                          Registered Geotechnical Engineers


                           Construction Site Safety
                        Pay for Safety Scheme


Introduction

              Construction works may inevitably entail risky activities.  Responsible
contractors should adopt safe work practices and provide necessary precautionary
measures to ensure construction sites under their charge are safe. Authorized persons,
registered structural engineers and registered geotechnical engineers are also required
under the Buildings Ordinance to ensure that building works under their supervisions
are carried out in a safe manner.

2.           While relevant parties should comply with the requirements on site safety
monitoring under the Technical Memorandum for Supervision Plans and the Code of
Practice for Site Supervision published by the Buildings Department, it is also important
to integrate site safety into the overall management responsibilities, to promote safety
training for all levels of the parties involved and to improve safety performance through
procurement and contractual arrangement.  As contractors are required to provide
continuous site supervisions and have the most prominent legal obligations to assure
construction site safety, they should have allowed in their tenders the cost of meeting
such obligations.  However, if such costs are not distinctly identified as safety-related
items for pricing, valuation and payment, resources allocated for the proper provision of
relevant measures may be undermined, thus jeopardising site safety.


Pay for Safety Scheme

3.           Pay for Safety Scheme (PFSS) introduced since 1996 specifically accords
proper identity to the cost for construction site safety. Under the PFSS, an employer is
obliged to pay the contractor upon the contractor’s satisfactory completion of the safety-
related items including training, as vetted and certified by the employer’s representative,
at the pre-priced rates set out in the Site Safety section in the Bills of Quantities or
Schedule of Rates.

4.          The following links are relevant:

          (a)   Construction  Site  Safety Manual  issued by  the Development
            Bureau
              (http://www.devb.gov.hk/en/publications_and_press_releases/publi
               cations/construction_site_safety_manual/index.html);



                                                                   /(b)…

          (b)   Factories  and  Industrial  Undertakings  (Safety  Management)
              Regulation (Cap 59AF) (http://www.elegislation.gov.hk/);

          (c)  The Real Estate Developers Association of Hong Kong and the
           Hong  Kong  Construction   Association’s  Safety   Partnering
            Programme (http://www.safetypartnering.com);

          (d)  Guidelines on  the Adoption  of  the Pay  for  Safety Scheme
              (http://www.cic.hk/cic_data/pdf/about_cic/publications/eng/PFSS_
               eng_final.pdf)  and  Reference  Materials on  Construction  Site
              Welfare, Health and Safety Measures (March 2017) (Chapter 7)
               (http://www.cic.hk/cic_data/pdf/about_cic/publications/eng/referen
              ce_materials/Site%20Welfare_booklet_e%20(final).pdf) published
            by the Construction Industry Council; and

          (e)   Safety training courses by the Occupational Safety and Health
              Training     Centre     of      the     Labour     Department
              (http://www.labour.gov.hk/eng/osh/content5.htm)            and
             Occupational       Safety      and       Health       Council
              (http://www.oshc.org.hk/eng/main/).

5.            Authorized Persons are encouraged to recommend your clients to adopt
the PFSS in construction contracts so as to flourish a fair and equitable environment for
the contracting parties to handle site safety issues.





                                (CHEUNG Tin-cheung)
                                                  Building Authority




Ref. : BD GR/1-115/10
